card.name: Estonian folk dance
card.era: Ancient circle/chain dances; systematized as 'rahvatants' early 20th c.; Dance Celebration from 1934
card.tagline: Estonia's umbrella folk-dance tradition, crowned by the Dance Celebration.
card.profile: Rahvatants is the broad umbrella of Estonian folk dance, encompassing ancient circle and chain dances, mimicry dances, set-dances, and couple dances such as the labajalavalss (flat-foot waltz, danced without rising onto the toes), kaerajaan, and tuljak (English Wikipedia; Kapper). Generally calm in character yet noted for a wide diversity of basic steps, it is typically accompanied by accordion, fiddle and other folk instruments. It is socially central to Estonian identity and concentrated in the Estonian Dance Celebration (Tantsupidu), first held in 1934 as the Dance and Gymnastic Festival within the first Estonian Games, now staged with the Song Celebration; UNESCO notes the tradition culminates in large-scale festivals every fifth year (English Wikipedia; UNESCO).
card.insight: Anna Raudkats's 1926 publication 'Eesti rahvatantsud' entrenched the idea that folk dances were old-fashioned village dances; the three most generally known - labajalavalss, kaerajaan and tuljak - are repeatedly cited as the canonical examples (Kapper, Folklore 54).

observation.setting: Indoor stage or hall with colored backdrop and wooden/smooth floor, and an outdoor grassy area with trees and rustic buildings.
observation.dancers: Mixed group of men and women of various ages, dancing in pairs and circles.
observation.formation_and_space: Pairs in a circle or scattered on the floor, holding hands in circle formations, and couples dancing together.
observation.posture: Upright torso, upright carriage with knees bent slightly during turns and steps.
observation.footwork: Quick side-to-side steps, hops, and turns on the beat; exact foot placement occluded by long skirts and low resolution.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held high in pairs, hand-in-hand circles, clapping overhead and in front of the body.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso upright with natural movement, no prominent hip isolations.
observation.partnering: Couples hold hands, spin together, and dance in closed or semi-open ballroom holds.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Frequent spinning turns by couples, small hops on feet, level remains upright with occasional lowering into bows.
observation.costume_and_props: Traditional Estonian folk costumes: women wear embroidered aprons and patterned skirts with head coverings; men wear dark jackets or vests, white shirts, knee-breeches or trousers, and hats.
observation.cannot_infer: Precise footwork details, weight distribution, and subtle upper body nuances are obscured by low video resolution and quick camera cuts.

signature_moments.what: Couples spinning rapidly in pairs with arms raised holding hands.
Large circle of dancers skipping sideways holding hands while clapping.
Dancers in dark skirts and white blouses performing interconnected arm-link turns in small groups.
